desc: Operates Indonesia's Gojek ride-hailing and delivery app, Tokopedia e-commerce marketplace and GoTo Financial payments services.
markets: Indonesia, with Gojek in Singapore and Vietnam earlier; merger talks with Grab have been reported but not completed.
rationale: Brand awareness among young Southeast Asian users and a showcase of its payments and super-app technology at Asian Grands Prix.

desc: Rents and manages vans, cars and fleets for UK businesses, formerly Redde Northgate, and provides accident management services.
markets: Almost entirely United Kingdom and Ireland, with fleet hire and accident management for corporate and insurer customers. No verified expansion plans.
rationale: B2B hospitality for fleet and insurer clients; limited consumer brand value, so a small-scale British Grand Prix hospitality play.

desc: Runs shared electric scooters and bikes in cities across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and the Middle East.
markets: Operates in around 30 countries with European cities its largest base; recently listed and expanding in Asia-Pacific and Middle East cities.
rationale: Urban-mobility brand could reach young city audiences at European and Miami races and promote micromobility partnerships with host cities.

desc: Operates the Budget car rental franchise in Saudi Arabia plus vehicle leasing and used-car sales.
markets: Saudi Arabia only, serving tourists, pilgrims and corporate fleets; growth tied to Vision 2030 tourism targets.
rationale: Saudi Grand Prix in Jeddah brings visitors who rent cars, giving a local activation and corporate hospitality angle.

desc: Operates Jahez, a food and grocery delivery app connecting restaurants, shops and couriers across Saudi Arabia.
markets: Saudi Arabia, with launches in Kuwait, Bahrain and Oman and pan-GCC expansion ambitions.
rationale: Consumer app could raise brand awareness among young Saudi and Gulf fans around the Jeddah and Qatar Grands Prix.

desc: Greek car rental and leasing group that also distributes Hertz franchise services and imports several car brands.
markets: Greece, Cyprus, Romania, Bulgaria and other Balkan markets; Hertz franchisee and vehicle importer with tourism-driven fleet growth.
rationale: Corporate hospitality for dealer and fleet customers; Hertz and car-brand ties offer a mobility link, but small international marketing footprint.

desc: Rents cars and trucks under the Hertz, Dollar and Thrifty brands at airports and city locations across the world.
markets: About 160 countries via franchises, with company-owned operations in the US, Canada, Europe and Australia; recent EV and Tesla fleet efforts.
rationale: Large consumer brand with a long motorsport heritage could host corporate customers and promote travel at US and European races.

desc: Brazilian company renting cars to consumers and fleets, selling used vehicles and operating Movida Franquias and subscription services.
markets: Brazil only, with fleet rental, subscription and used-car dealerships; no international operations known.
rationale: Brazil's Sao Paulo Grand Prix offers a home-market platform for brand awareness and fleet-customer hospitality.

desc: Chinese online grocery retailer using front-warehouse delivery to bring fresh produce to households in Shanghai and nearby cities.
markets: Mainland China, concentrated in Yangtze River Delta cities; no overseas operations known.
rationale: Brand-building at the Shanghai Grand Prix is possible but consumer grocery marketing is local and F1 fit is limited.

desc: Operates taxis, limousines, buses and delivery bikes in Dubai under the Dubai Taxi and Careem Bike names.
markets: Dubai and the wider UAE, with airport transport and franchise licences; limited foreign operations.
rationale: Abu Dhabi Grand Prix visitors and Gulf hospitality guests provide a natural transport sponsorship, though marketing scale is modest.

desc: Runs online travel brands Booking.com, Priceline, Agoda, Kayak and OpenTable, selling hotel, flight and rental bookings worldwide.
markets: Operates in over 200 countries, strongest in Europe; growth in Asia via Agoda and in transport and payments.
rationale: Global consumer brand could use race calendar travel demand and fan trip packages to promote bookings across European and Asian markets.

desc: Operates the Airbnb online marketplace for short-term home rentals, experiences and services in more than 220 countries.
markets: Listings in over 220 countries; recent expansion into services and experiences and into markets such as India and China.
rationale: Host-city race weekends strain hotel supply, making Airbnb a natural accommodation partner and a way to promote experiences globally.

desc: Operates Royal Caribbean, Celebrity Cruises and Silversea cruise lines plus private destinations such as Perfect Day at CocoCay.
markets: Cruises sold worldwide with Caribbean, Europe and Asia itineraries; new ships and private-island destinations planned.
rationale: Premium cruise brand can offer fan cruise packages and hospitality at Monaco, Miami and Singapore, where its ships already call.

desc: Operates Viking river and ocean cruises and expedition ships for older, affluent travellers, with sailings across Europe and worldwide.
markets: Ocean and river ships across Europe, Asia, Americas and Antarctica; new ships and Mississippi, Nile and Mekong expansion.
rationale: Affluent, travel-minded audience matches F1 fan demographics; sponsorship could promote European river cruises around Monaco and other races.

desc: Operates cruise lines Carnival, Princess, Holland America, Cunard and Costa, serving North American and European passengers.
markets: Major markets in North America, Europe and Australia; new ships and Celebration Key private island in the Bahamas.
rationale: Mass-market cruise brand could reach US fans at Miami and Las Vegas, and sell race-weekend cruise packages.

desc: Operates Expedia, Hotels.com, Vrbo and Expedia Partner Solutions, selling travel bookings to consumers and travel businesses.
markets: Operates in around 70 countries; B2B platform sells to airlines and banks, and growth in Asia is a focus.
rationale: B2B hospitality for partner travel businesses and brand awareness for Vrbo with fans travelling to US and European races.

desc: China's largest online travel agency, selling hotels, flights and packages, with international brands Trip.com, Skyscanner and Ctrip.
markets: Strong in China; Trip.com serves outbound travellers in Asia, Europe and the Middle East, with Skyscanner adding international reach.
rationale: Chinese outbound travel demand could be reached at the Shanghai race and with overseas fans visiting Grands Prix.

desc: Provides corporate travel management, expense and meetings services to business customers and travel managers worldwide.
markets: Operates in more than 140 countries, serving large corporate clients and growing after acquiring CWT.
rationale: B2B hospitality and corporate event travel make F1 a client-entertainment platform; company is a partner of American Express.

desc: India's leading online travel agency, selling flights, hotels, buses, trains and holiday packages through MakeMyTrip, goibibo and redBus.
markets: India with outbound travel and hotel inventory across Asia and the Middle East; growth in Gulf visitor markets.
rationale: Rising Indian interest in F1 and outbound travel suggests promoting Grand Prix trip packages to Indian fans.

desc: Operates package holidays, hotels, cruises and tour activities for customers mainly in Germany, the United Kingdom and Nordic countries.
markets: Operates across Europe with hotels such as RIU, Robinson and TUI Blue and cruise ships; expanding online and digital sales.
rationale: European fan travel packages and hospitality for race weekends, with a large customer base across Germany, the UK and Nordics.

desc: Runs online train ticketing, railway catering and tourism services, including Maharajas' Express and luxury tourist trains for Indian Railways.
markets: India only, with limited international tourism promotion; owned by Indian Railways.
rationale: Weak commercial fit; a state tourism body, but luxury train and hospitality offers could target affluent Indian F1 fans.

desc: Operates expedition cruises and Natural Habitat adventure travel to Antarctica, the Galapagos, Alaska and other remote destinations.
markets: Voyages in polar regions, Galapagos and Europe, with National Geographic partnership; adding ships and land-based travel.
rationale: Affluent explorer audience is a niche fit; sponsorship would be small-scale and brand-led at selected races.

desc: Operates the Hotelbeds B2B platform connecting hotels and activities with travel agencies and airlines for bookings worldwide.
markets: Sells hotel inventory in more than 170 countries to travel agents and tour operators; growth in Asia and the Americas.
rationale: B2B hospitality value for travel agent clients but it is a business platform with no consumer brand to promote.

desc: Sells cruises and holidays plus insurance and financial products to British customers aged over 50 under the Saga brand.
markets: Mainly United Kingdom, with river and ocean cruises sold to British travellers; no verified expansion plans.
rationale: Older British audience at British Grand Prix has some overlap, but F1 fit is weak for a domestic over-50s brand.

desc: Sells leisure and corporate travel through Flight Centre, Corporate Traveller and FCM brands in Australia, Europe, the Americas and Asia.
markets: Operations in about 10 countries; focus on corporate travel growth in the UK, US, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Australian Grand Prix and corporate hospitality offer brand exposure; F1 travel packages could be sold through its stores and corporate arm.

desc: Operates Saudi travel businesses including Almosafer travel agency, Mawasim and Tajawal, serving tourists, pilgrims and corporate travel.
markets: Saudi Arabia and Gulf, with online and offline services; targets growth in inbound tourism under Vision 2030.
rationale: Saudi Grand Prix provides visitor flows and hospitality for corporate clients, supporting Seera's inbound tourism focus.

desc: Sells flights, hotels and holiday packages to Australian and New Zealand consumers through the Webjet online booking site.
markets: Australia and New Zealand; online consumer travel with no verified expansion plans after separation from the B2B Hotelbeds business.
rationale: Australian Grand Prix could provide a consumer travel promotion, but marketing budgets are modest.

desc: French tour operator selling tailor-made adventure and cultural trips, with Voyageurs du Monde, Nomade Aventure and other brands.
markets: Mainly France, with some Belgium and Switzerland; sells trips to destinations worldwide to French-speaking travellers.
rationale: French Grand Prix absence and niche premium audience make F1 a weak fit, although Monaco hospitality is a possibility.

desc: Operates TripAdvisor travel review website, Viator tours and TheFork restaurant booking, connecting travellers with experiences and bookings.
markets: Over 40 markets; growth in Viator experiences and restaurant booking in Europe.
rationale: Global consumer travel brand can feature race-city experiences and promote Viator tours across fans traveling to Grand Prix venues.

desc: Online ticketing platform selling rail and coach tickets across the UK and Europe through Trainline app and website.
markets: United Kingdom, France, Italy, Spain and other European countries; developing business-to-business platform for rail operators.
rationale: Rail travel to European races fits Trainline's customer base, especially for Silverstone, Spa and Monza, but marketing scale is moderate.

desc: Sells flights and hotels to consumers in Europe and the US through the eDreams, GO Voyages, Opodo and Travellink brands.
markets: Operates in around 30 countries across Europe, the US and Asia, with Prime subscription growth.
rationale: Subscription travel brand could target European fans of Spanish and Monaco races and cross-sell flights to Grand Prix.

desc: Operates ferries and cruise ships between Estonia, Finland, Sweden and Latvia, plus hotels and shops on board.
markets: Baltic Sea routes linking Estonia, Finland, Sweden and Latvia; no overseas operations or verified expansion.
rationale: Weak fit; regional ferry marketing and domestic customers, though Nordic hospitality packages are conceivable.

desc: Japanese travel agency selling overseas and domestic tours through H.I.S. branches, and operating Huis Ten Bosch resort and hotels.
markets: Japan with offices across Asia, Europe and the Americas; hotels and energy business expansion.
rationale: Japanese fans travel to Suzuka and abroad, giving a natural travel-package promotion, though group marketing is modest.

desc: Provides corporate travel management and event services to business customers in Australia, Asia, Europe and North America.
markets: Operations in the Asia-Pacific, Europe and North America after expanding via acquisition of Travel and Transport.
rationale: Corporate event and hospitality services fit client entertainment at races, but brand has limited consumer appeal.

desc: Operates the trivago hotel price-comparison website and app in more than 50 countries.
markets: Available in over 50 countries and 30 languages; focus on performance marketing in Europe, the US and Asia.
rationale: Hotel comparison for Grand Prix cities fits a consumer travel brand aiming to reach a global fan audience.

desc: Online travel group selling flights, hotels and holiday packages through lastminute.com, Volagratis, Rumbo and Hotelopia.
markets: Operates in Europe with Italy, Spain, UK and Germany; moves into tour operator Hotelopia and cruise offerings.
rationale: Last-minute European travel brand could promote race weekend packages for fans, but sponsor budgets are small.

desc: Operates a major US airline with domestic and international passenger and cargo services, plus Delta Vacations and regional partners.
markets: Hubs in Atlanta, Detroit, Minneapolis and New York, with partnerships with Air France-KLM, Virgin Atlantic and LATAM.
rationale: Premium traveller base suits B2B hospitality and US race travel from Miami, Austin and Las Vegas; strong brand potential.

desc: Promotes concerts and operates venues and Ticketmaster, selling tickets for live music, sports and events around the world.
markets: Operates in over 40 countries with festivals and venues; expanding in Asia, Latin America and Middle East.
rationale: Live events and ticketing synergy with Grand Prix weekends and concerts, with global audience and sponsorship sales business.

desc: Operates Tokyo Disney Resort, including the theme parks, hotels and monorail, under licence from Disney.
markets: Japan only, with plans to build a new theme park in Chiba; guests are largely domestic.
rationale: Weak overseas marketing need, though hospitality and Suzuka-related brand tie-ins are possible.

desc: Operates a large US airline with international hubs and Star Alliance membership, flying passengers and cargo worldwide.
markets: Hubs in Chicago, Newark, San Francisco, Houston, Denver, Los Angeles and Washington Dulles; expanding in Europe and Asia routes.
rationale: Premium US carrier with business travellers fits hospitality at Miami, Austin and Las Vegas, and international race routes.

desc: Operates Europe's largest low-cost airline, flying short-haul routes across Europe and North Africa with a focus on low fares.
markets: Over 40 countries in Europe and North Africa, growing capacity in Poland, Italy, Spain and Morocco.
rationale: Low-cost fares can reach fans travelling to European races, but brand marketing is price-led and sponsorship culture is light.

desc: Franchises and manages hotels including InterContinental, Holiday Inn, Crowne Plaza and Kimpton in more than 100 countries.
markets: Over 6,500 hotels in more than 100 countries; strong growth in Greater China and brand expansion.
rationale: Hospitality partner for race-weekend accommodation across Grand Prix cities and loyalty programme promotion to global fans.

desc: Holding company for British Airways, Iberia, Vueling, Aer Lingus and Level, flying transatlantic and European routes.
markets: Hubs in London, Madrid, Barcelona, Dublin and Paris; transatlantic network and expansion in Latin America and Asia.
rationale: British Airways hub for London and Madrid races, premium cabin B2B hospitality and global brand reach among F1 fans.

desc: Runs India's largest airline, operating low-cost domestic and international flights to Asia, Middle East and Europe.
markets: Domestic India plus rapidly growing long-haul routes to Europe and Asia, with widebody fleet planned.
rationale: India lacks a Grand Prix yet; sponsorship could build brand with affluent Indian fans travelling to Singapore and Abu Dhabi.

desc: Operates a low-cost US airline with domestic network and some routes to Caribbean, Mexico and Central America.
markets: US and nearby Caribbean and Latin America; adding assigned seating and premium cabin options.
rationale: US domestic fans of Austin and Miami races fit, but the brand is value-focused with limited international marketing.

desc: China's flag carrier operating domestic and international passenger and cargo flights from Beijing and other hubs, in Star Alliance.
markets: Hubs in Beijing and Chengdu; routes to Europe, North America and Asia, with Shenzhen Airlines and Air Macau units.
rationale: Chinese Grand Prix in Shanghai and overseas Chinese travellers give limited but plausible reach, and state ownership narrows marketing.

desc: Operates and franchises Chinese hotel brands Hanting, Ji, Orange and Blue Sky, with Steigenberger Hotels in Germany.
markets: China and Europe via Steigenberger and Deutsche Hospitality; adding hotels across Asia and the Middle East.
rationale: Hotel network in Shanghai and European Grand Prix cities offers hospitality tie-ins for Chinese and German fans.

desc: China Southern is one of Asia's largest airlines, operating a large domestic and international passenger network from Guangzhou.
markets: Hub in Guangzhou with routes to Europe, Australia and North America; member of SkyTeam.
rationale: Reaches Chinese travellers going to F1 races; state ownership and domestic focus limit marketing alignment.

desc: Largest airline group in South America, operating domestic and international passenger and cargo flights across Latin America.
markets: Chile, Peru, Brazil, Colombia and Ecuador, with routes to Europe, the US and Oceania; Delta partnership.
rationale: Reaches Latin American fans travelling to Sao Paulo, Mexico City and Miami races, supporting brand awareness and B2B hospitality.

desc: Operates and franchises hotels including Sofitel, Novotel, ibis and Raffles, and runs the ALL loyalty programme and Sport marketing.
markets: Over 5,000 hotels in more than 110 countries; luxury and lifestyle expansion and global sports sponsorships.
rationale: Hotel brands and ALL loyalty programme link well with race-weekend travel, and Accor already sponsors major sports teams.

desc: Owns Taj, Vivanta and Ginger hotels in India and abroad, part of the Tata Group.
markets: India with properties in the Middle East, Southeast Asia, Europe and the US; targeting 700 hotels by 2030.
rationale: Luxury hospitality for affluent Indian and Gulf guests could pair with Tata brands, though F1 history is limited.

desc: Group of Lufthansa, Swiss, Austrian, Brussels and Eurowings airlines, plus cargo and technical services across Europe and worldwide.
markets: Hubs in Frankfurt, Munich, Zurich, Vienna and Brussels; investing in ITA Airways and network growth in Asia.
rationale: Premium airline can offer VIP travel for race hospitality, with strong European fan base and German Grand Prix interest.

desc: Hong Kong-based international airline flying passengers and cargo from Hong Kong to Asia, Europe, North America and Australia.
markets: Hub in Hong Kong with Oneworld alliance partners and cargo network; restoring long-haul and Mainland China routes.
rationale: Premium travellers and Asia network make it a candidate for Singapore, Japan and China race hospitality and brand building.

desc: Chinese state-owned airline flying domestic and international passenger routes from Shanghai Pudong and Hongqiao, a SkyTeam member.
markets: Hubs in Shanghai with routes across Asia, Europe, North America and Australia.
rationale: Hometown airline of the Chinese Grand Prix in Shanghai, with potential to reach Chinese fans travelling to races.

desc: Operates large Life Time athletic country clubs and digital health services, with memberships across the United States and Canada.
markets: US and Canada, with premium clubs and new openings; offers digital app and events like Life Time Miami Marathon.
rationale: Affluent members and high-end health brand could support US race activations and performance-themed content in Miami and Austin.

desc: Operates Australia's flag-carrier airline Qantas and low-cost Jetstar, flying domestic and international passenger and freight routes.
markets: Australia network with long-haul flights to Asia, Europe and North America, including Project Sunrise non-stop flights.
rationale: Australian Grand Prix partner potential in Melbourne, and Qantas Frequent Flyer links reach fans travelling to Asian races.

desc: Japan's flag carrier operating domestic and international passenger and cargo flights, member of Oneworld, with low-cost arm Zipair.
markets: Hubs at Tokyo Haneda and Narita; international routes to North America, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Suzuka host race and premium travellers fit, offering brand building with Japanese fans and global visitors.

desc: Real estate investment trust owning Gaylord convention hotels and entertainment venues, including the Grand Ole Opry in Nashville.
markets: United States only, with large convention resorts in Nashville, Florida, Texas and Colorado.
rationale: Corporate group hospitality and events overlap with F1 but the company is a US real estate trust with little consumer marketing.

desc: Japanese airline group operating ANA full-service and Peach low-cost flights, domestic and international, in Star Alliance.
markets: Hubs at Tokyo Haneda and Narita with routes to Asia, North America and Europe; plans for new aircraft and routes.
rationale: Suzuka race and premium business travellers make ANA a strong candidate for hospitality and Japanese market branding.

desc: Turkey's flag carrier, flying to more destinations than any other airline from its Istanbul hub, with cargo and technical services.
markets: Over 350 destinations in more than 130 countries; Istanbul Airport hub and aircraft order of several hundred planes.
rationale: Global reach and past Istanbul Park Grand Prix make Turkish a strong candidate for brand building in Europe, Asia and Africa.

desc: Operates American Airlines, a large US carrier with hubs in Dallas, Charlotte, Miami and Chicago and Oneworld membership.
markets: Network across the Americas, Europe and Asia; hubs in Miami and Dallas close to US Grand Prix.
rationale: Premium traveller base and Miami and Austin race locations support hospitality and promotional tie-ins.

desc: Chinese airline group operating Hainan Airlines flights, listed through B-shares in Shanghai, with domestic and international routes.
markets: Hubs at Haikou and Beijing, routes across Asia, Europe and North America.
rationale: Plausible tie to Chinese Grand Prix but private-ownership and domestic marketing focus limit F1 fit.

desc: Korea's flag carrier operating passenger and cargo flights from Seoul Incheon, merged with Asiana Airlines.
markets: Hub at Incheon with routes across Asia, Europe, Americas; SkyTeam member integrating Asiana and low-cost carriers.
rationale: Premium cabin and Korean fans travelling to Singapore and Japan make hospitality and brand sponsorship plausible.

desc: Taiwanese airline operating passenger and cargo flights from Taoyuan to Asia, North America and Europe, in Star Alliance.
markets: Hub at Taoyuan with routes across Asia, US and Europe, and Hello Kitty branded planes.
rationale: Premium Taiwanese carrier could build brand with travelling fans at Asian races, but marketing budget is modest.

desc: Operates low-cost flights across Europe from bases in the UK, France, Italy, Germany and other countries, plus easyJet Holidays.
markets: Over 35 countries in Europe and North Africa, with easyJet holidays growth.
rationale: Reaches British and European fans travelling to races, and easyJet Holidays can sell Grand Prix packages.

desc: Aircraft lessor owning and leasing commercial jets to airlines worldwide, with offices in Singapore, Dublin, Seattle and Tianjin.
markets: Leases to airlines in around 50 countries; Chinese Bank of China owned and a Singapore Grand Prix home market.
rationale: Business-to-business brand with airline customers; hospitality use only, with limited consumer relevance.
flags: majority-owned subsidiary of Bank of China

desc: Ticketing and live entertainment group running Eventim ticket platforms and promoter businesses, mainly in Germany and Europe.
markets: Europe's leading ticketing platform with operations in Germany, UK, Italy, Spain and other countries, including venue operations.
rationale: Ticketing and hospitality sales for European races and live events, supporting event business with a Grand Prix partner role.

desc: Chinese low-cost airline flying domestic routes and short-haul international flights across Asia from Shanghai and other hubs.
markets: China with routes to Japan, South Korea, Thailand, Singapore and other Asian destinations.
rationale: Shanghai-based carrier could target Chinese fans for the Chinese Grand Prix, but price-focused marketing limits F1 fit.

desc: Owns and operates Premier Inn hotels in the UK and Germany, with restaurants such as Brewers Fayre.
markets: United Kingdom and Germany, with rapid expansion of Premier Inn hotels in German cities.
rationale: Premier Inn near Silverstone and German expansion offer accommodation partnerships for fans, but it is a value-focused brand.

desc: Japanese holding company operating Seibu railways, Prince Hotels, resorts, real estate and ski areas.
markets: Mostly Japan with Prince Hotels and resorts; some hotels abroad and inbound tourism.
rationale: Suzuka-related hospitality and inbound-tourism marketing are possible, but it is mainly a domestic rail and property company.
flags: holding / investment vehicle, not an operating brand

desc: Franchises hotel brands including Wyndham, Ramada, Days Inn and La Quinta, with thousands of properties across 95 countries.
markets: About 9,000 hotels in around 95 countries; international growth in EMEA and Asia Pacific.
rationale: Economy and midscale hotels near race venues provide fan accommodation, and loyalty programme promotion is possible.

desc: Operates Copa Airlines and Wingo from Panama City, connecting Latin America with North America and the Caribbean.
markets: Hub in Panama City serving more than 80 destinations across the Americas.
rationale: Connects Latin American fans to Mexico City, Miami and Sao Paulo races, but sponsorship culture is limited.

desc: Operates ski resorts such as Vail, Whistler, Park City and Breckenridge, and sells Epic Pass seasonal passes.
markets: Resorts in the US, Canada, Australia, Switzerland and Japan.
rationale: Affluent customer base and winter lifestyle brand could pair with Austin and Montreal races, though overlap is modest.

desc: Franchises hotel brands such as Comfort, Quality Inn, Clarion and Cambria across the United States and abroad.
markets: Over 7,000 hotels in about 45 countries, with expansion in Europe and Asia via franchise growth.
rationale: Midscale brands could sell race-weekend accommodation, and loyalty member marketing to US fans.

desc: Operates and franchises mid-to-upscale hotels such as Atour, Atour Light, Zhotel and retail sales of sleep products in China.
markets: China, with hotel network growing and retail business; no major overseas expansion yet.
rationale: Shanghai Grand Prix lodging and Chinese consumer brand building, though the brand is mainly domestic.

desc: Operates Poland's largest fitness club network and the MultiSport card, and provides fitness subscription to employees in several countries.
markets: Poland, Czech Republic, Slovakia, Bulgaria, Croatia and Turkey; expanding the MultiSport card in Central Europe.
rationale: Brand-building among Central European employers and active consumers; limited F1 link beyond sports marketing in region.

desc: Diversified Canadian company owning regional airlines and aerospace and manufacturing businesses, including Calm Air, PAL Airlines and Quest.
markets: Canada plus operations in the US, Europe and the Caribbean through acquisitions.
rationale: Business-to-business company with low consumer marketing needs; a Montreal Grand Prix tie-in is possible but weak.

desc: Operates vacation ownership and exchange businesses Wyndham Destinations, RCI and Travel + Leisure Co. brand club memberships.
markets: US-focused timeshare with resorts in Europe, Mexico and Caribbean, and RCI exchange network in more than 100 countries.
rationale: Hospitality and travel club membership could pair with race-weekend packages and loyalty promotions for members.

desc: Operates movie theatres in the United States and Latin America under Cinemark and Century brands.
markets: United States and Latin America including Brazil, Chile, Colombia and Peru.
rationale: F1 screenings and movie tie-ins could use cinemas as fan venues; marketing alignment is moderate.

desc: Franchises Planet Fitness gyms with low-price memberships across North America and some international markets.
markets: US, Canada, Mexico, Panama and Australia, plus new clubs in Spain and other markets.
rationale: Mass-market gym brand could target casual fans with fitness content, but F1 is not core.

desc: Owns the Sphere venue in Las Vegas and MSG Networks, hosting immersive shows and concerts.
markets: Las Vegas Sphere with planned venues in Abu Dhabi and other cities, and MSG Networks in New York.
rationale: Sphere is a showcase for immersive content and hospitality in Las Vegas, which hosts an F1 Grand Prix.

desc: Taiwan's flag carrier operating passenger and cargo flights from Taoyuan to Asia, North America, Europe and Oceania, in SkyTeam.
markets: Hub at Taoyuan with routes across Asia, US and Europe, and a large cargo business.
rationale: Premium travellers and Asian race travel make hospitality possible; Taiwan has no Grand Prix of its own.

desc: Operates Alaska Airlines and Hawaiian Airlines, flying domestic and Pacific routes mainly on the US West Coast.
markets: US West Coast, Hawaii, Mexico, Costa Rica, and new international long-haul flights to Asia and Europe from Seattle.
rationale: West Coast fans going to Las Vegas, Austin and Miami races could be reached, with premium corporate hospitality.

desc: Thailand's flag carrier flying passengers and cargo from Bangkok to Asia, Europe, Australia and the US, in Star Alliance.
markets: Hub at Suvarnabhumi with routes across Asia, Europe, Australia, and recovery after bankruptcy rehabilitation.
rationale: Thailand tourism promotion and fans travelling to Singapore and other Asian races support brand-building.

desc: Holding company for Air France, KLM, Transavia and Martinair, with hubs in Paris and Amsterdam and SkyTeam membership.
markets: Network across Europe, Africa, Asia and the Americas via Paris and Amsterdam hubs; partnership with Delta.
rationale: European hubs link fans to Monaco, Spa and Zandvoort, and premium cabins fit hospitality sponsorship.

desc: Vietnam's largest low-cost airline, operating domestic and international flights across Southeast Asia, North Asia and Australia.
markets: Vietnam with routes to Singapore, Thailand, Korea, Japan, India, Australia; expanding aircraft fleet and European routes.
rationale: Brand-building for Vietnamese and Asian travellers around a possible Hanoi Grand Prix history and Singapore race.

desc: Canada's largest airline, operating domestic and international passenger and cargo flights, with Aeroplan loyalty programme, in Star Alliance.
markets: Hubs in Toronto, Montreal and Vancouver with routes to Europe, Asia and the Americas.
rationale: Montreal-based carrier with a natural fit for the Canadian Grand Prix, and Aeroplan promotions with fans.

desc: Operates vacation ownership and exchange, including Marriott Vacation Club, Westin and Sheraton Vacation Club, under licences from Marriott.
markets: Resorts across the US, Caribbean, Europe and Asia; sells vacation ownership under licensed Marriott and Hyatt brands.
rationale: Marriott-licensed holiday ownership could use race weekends in Miami and Europe for lead generation with affluent travellers.
f1: Licensee of Marriott brands (Marriott Bonvoy is a Formula 1 partner); not a Marriott subsidiary

desc: Israel's flag carrier operating passenger and cargo flights from Tel Aviv to Europe, North America and Asia.
markets: Hub at Ben Gurion Airport with routes to Europe, US and Far East; adding new aircraft.
rationale: Limited F1 fit given security and geography, though affluent travellers to Europe could be targeted.

desc: Operates hotels, restaurants and food brands, including Minor Hotels, Anantara, Avani and The Pizza Company, in Thailand and worldwide.
markets: Hotels in more than 60 countries; restaurants and lifestyle brands, with NH Hotel Group ownership.
rationale: Anantara and NH Hotel brands could provide luxury accommodation at Grand Prix cities; Thai market also hosts F1 events.

desc: Operates Jet2 airline and Jet2holidays, selling package holidays from UK airports to Mediterranean and European destinations.
markets: United Kingdom to Mediterranean and European short-haul and city-break destinations; expanding bases and fleet.
rationale: British holiday audience and race-weekend packages are possible, but marketing is value-focused.

desc: Israeli hotel group operating Fattal Hotels and Leonardo Hotels, with hundreds of hotels across Israel and Europe.
markets: Israel and Europe, especially Germany, the UK and Netherlands via Leonardo; expansion in Europe.
rationale: Leonardo hotels in European race cities could provide accommodation partnerships, though brand marketing is modest.

desc: Sells and manages vacation ownership under Hilton Grand Vacations, Diamond Resorts and Bluegreen brands.
markets: Resorts in the US, Europe, Asia and Caribbean; sells timeshare memberships mainly to US customers.
rationale: Hilton-licensed vacation ownership offers a lead-generation platform at US and European races for affluent travellers.
f1: Licensee of Hilton brand (Hilton is a Formula 1 official partner); not a Hilton subsidiary

desc: Operates NH Hotels, NH Collection and Nhow hotels in Europe and Latin America, owned by Minor International.
markets: Hotels in Europe and Latin America, mainly Spain, Italy, Germany and Netherlands; owned by Minor International.
rationale: City hotels near Spanish, Dutch, Italian and Monaco races offer accommodation partnerships, but marketing is regional.

desc: Operates regional airline SkyWest, flying capacity for Delta, United, American and Alaska on short-haul US routes.
markets: United States and Canada, flying under capacity agreements for major airlines.
rationale: No consumer brand, so F1 sponsorship offers little commercial benefit.

desc: Operates AMC Theatres, the largest cinema chain in the world, with locations in the United States and Europe.
markets: United States plus Odeon and UCI cinemas across the UK and Europe.
rationale: F1 film screenings and watch parties could use theatres, but sponsorship budgets are limited.

desc: Spanish hotel group operating Meliá, Gran Meliá, Paradisus and ME resorts, with many in Europe, Caribbean and Asia.
markets: Hotels in more than 40 countries; focus on Spain, Latin America, Caribbean, with growth in Asia and Middle East.
rationale: Spanish resort brand could host fans at Barcelona, Miami and Gulf races, and reach premium leisure travellers.

desc: Vietnam's flag carrier operating domestic and international passenger and cargo flights, in SkyTeam.
markets: Hubs in Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City with routes across Asia, Europe, Australia and the US.
rationale: Vietnam tourism promotion and Singapore race travellers provide possible brand building, but carrier is state-owned.

desc: Operates Aeromexico, Mexico's flag carrier, flying domestic and international routes and cargo, in SkyTeam.
markets: Hubs in Mexico City with routes to the US, Latin America, Europe and Asia; Delta partnership.
rationale: Mexico City Grand Prix is the strongest local F1 event, offering hospitality and brand benefits.

desc: Low-cost US airline flying leisure travellers from smaller cities to Las Vegas, Florida and other vacation destinations, plus Sunseeker resort.
markets: United States only, with leisure routes to Las Vegas, Orlando and other destinations.
rationale: Las Vegas Grand Prix could attract leisure travellers, but airline marketing is price-focused and domestic.

desc: Japanese operator of membership resort hotels, wedding venues and medical-membership services under Resorttrust and Grand Bach brands.
markets: Japan only, with membership resorts and hotels; few overseas operations.
rationale: Affluent members and hospitality focus offer a modest Suzuka angle, but limited marketing culture.

desc: Brazilian low-cost airline operating domestic flights and international routes in South America, part of Abra Group.
markets: Brazil and South America, with routes to the US and Caribbean; owned by Abra Group.
rationale: Brazilian Grand Prix in Sao Paulo makes it a natural local fit for brand building, although finances are restructured.

desc: Operates Dormy Inn business hotels and company dormitories in Japan, along with resort hotels and some overseas sites.
markets: Japan, with some hotels in Korea and Vietnam; no verified expansion plans.
rationale: Weak F1 fit; domestic business hotels with limited marketing, although Suzuka accommodation is plausible.

desc: Owns and operates luxury hotels and resorts under Shangri-La, Kerry and Traders brands across Asia, Europe and the Middle East.
markets: Hotels in China, Southeast Asia, Europe, Middle East and Australia; new hotel openings in Asia.
rationale: Luxury hotels in Singapore, Shanghai and Abu Dhabi could host high-end hospitality and brand placement.

desc: Saudi low-cost airline operating flynas flights between domestic cities and destinations in the Middle East, Europe and Asia.
markets: Saudi Arabia with routes to Gulf, Egypt, Europe, Turkey and South Asia; new aircraft orders.
rationale: Saudi Grand Prix in Jeddah matches its home market and fan travel, offering local brand building.

desc: Operates SeaWorld, Busch Gardens and Sesame Place theme parks across the United States.
markets: United States only, concentrated in Florida, Texas, Virginia and California; no verified international expansion.
rationale: Family-oriented parks could use Miami weekend promotions, but F1 audience overlap is small.

desc: Operates Soho House private members clubs, hotels and restaurants in London, New York, Los Angeles and other major cities.
markets: Clubs in Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East; planning more Soho Houses and Soho Works.
rationale: Affluent creative members suit hospitality events during London, Miami and Monaco weekends, and F1 culture is popular with members.

desc: Operates Frontier Airlines, an ultra-low-cost US carrier flying domestic and Latin American routes.
markets: United States, Mexico, Caribbean and Latin America; adding routes from Denver and other bases.
rationale: Value-led marketing and low fares limit F1 fit, though fan travel to Miami and Austin could be targeted.

desc: Owns hotels, catering and exhibition businesses in Abu Dhabi, including Le Royal Meridien and the Abu Dhabi National Exhibition Centre.
markets: Abu Dhabi and UAE, with hospitality management; local event business at ADNEC.
rationale: Abu Dhabi Grand Prix is its home race, giving hospitality, catering and exhibition business opportunities.

desc: Provides helicopter services, aircraft charter, maintenance and training for oil and gas, medevac and government clients in the UAE.
markets: Abu Dhabi, UAE and Gulf, with some international contracts in Africa and Asia.
rationale: Helicopter and charter services could support Abu Dhabi Grand Prix VIP transport but marketing is limited.

desc: Operates low-cost airline Wizz Air, flying from Central and Eastern Europe to destinations across Europe and the Middle East.
markets: Central and Eastern Europe, Italy, UK and Middle East, expanding with Abu Dhabi and new long-haul aircraft orders.
rationale: Fans travelling to Hungarian, Italian and Gulf races could be reached, though brand is price-led.

desc: Turkish low-cost airline Pegasus, flying domestic and international routes from Istanbul Sabiha Gokcen to Europe, Middle East and Asia.
markets: Turkey, Europe, Middle East, Central Asia; ongoing fleet expansion with Airbus orders.
rationale: Past Istanbul race and young leisure audience offer brand potential, but low-cost marketing limits F1 value.

desc: Operates Virgin Australia airline, flying domestic and some international routes with Velocity Frequent Flyer, partly owned by Qatar Airways.
markets: Australia with routes to New Zealand, Fiji, Bali and Qatar via Qatar Airways partnership.
rationale: Australian Grand Prix and its Qatar Airways partner give plausible tie-ins, with Velocity members as target.

desc: Operates Norwegian Air Shuttle, a low-cost airline flying across the Nordic countries and Europe.
markets: Norway, Sweden, Denmark, Finland, plus European leisure routes and Spain; no long-haul flights currently.
rationale: Nordic fans travelling to European races could be reached, but marketing scope is modest.

desc: Operates JetBlue Airways, a US carrier focused on New York, Boston and Florida, flying domestic, Caribbean and transatlantic routes.
markets: US, Caribbean, Latin America, plus London and Paris routes from New York and Boston.
rationale: Reaches US fans travelling to Miami and Montreal races; JetBlue Mint premium cabin supports hospitality.

desc: Korean airline operating passenger and cargo flights across Asia, Europe, and North America, now controlled by Korean Air.
markets: Hubs at Incheon with routes across Asia, US and Europe, being integrated into Korean Air.
rationale: Limited standalone marketing as integration with Korean Air proceeds.
flags: majority-owned subsidiary of Korean Air Lines

desc: Finland's flag carrier, flying passengers and cargo between Europe and Asia via Helsinki, in Oneworld.
markets: Helsinki hub linking Europe with Asia; focus on Nordic and leisure routes.
rationale: Finnish fans and a Helsinki gateway could support Nordic brand building, though marketing is limited.

desc: Operates Six Flags and Cedar Fair amusement parks across the United States, Canada and Mexico, selling season passes and tickets.
markets: North America only, with 40-plus parks; no verified international expansion beyond licensing in the Middle East.
rationale: Theme park brand has family reach, but F1 fit is weak and mostly for local activations.

desc: Greece's largest airline, operating domestic and international flights from Athens and other hubs, a member of Star Alliance.
markets: Greece with routes across Europe and the Middle East; adding aircraft.
rationale: Tourism marketing for Greece and fans travelling to Monaco and Italy, but sponsorship culture is limited.

desc: Operates ski resorts and leisure parks including Parc Asterix, Futuroscope and Grevin museums, mainly in France.
markets: Mainly France with ski areas in the Alps and leisure parks; minor operations abroad.
rationale: Regional French audience and no Grand Prix in France limit appeal, though Monaco hospitality is possible.
